subject: Ironridge on-site cluster blueprint and IO handoff
messages:
From: Danielle Park <danielle@ironridge.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Ironridge on-site cluster intake: hardware inventory + first-run asks

Hi Mateo —

Thanks again for taking the call earlier. Per our conversation, attaching the current hardware inventory and a rough rack map (see attachments). We’re planning a small POC at our Palo Alto site to validate private deployment (VPC-connected site with optional air-gapped mode later). High-level asks: 

- Recommended node pool mix for a 3‑rack compact cluster (GPU: 2x A100 per rack planned; CPU: mix of 24-core and 48-core nodes). 
- Persistent storage strategy: NVMe local + central blockstore? What should we use for model checkpoints vs ephemeral KV cache?
- Networking: we have a single /22 private VLAN block per site; we need guidance for control-plane segregation, egress breakouts, and cross-connect to our VPC via AWS Direct Connect.
- Security/compliance: KMS integration for key wrapping (we use HashiCorp Vault), audit-log retention for 90 days.

Constraints and notes:
- We need a plan that fits a 2U per GPU chassis profile; limited power per rack (max 12kW) so node count may be limited.
- We may need to maintain an option to run the control-plane on dedicated machines without GPUs.

Attachments: ironridge-hw-inventory.csv, site-network-diagram-v1.pdf, initial-provisioning-playbook.md

Can you share a short blueprint and an initial checklist we can review before the on-site discovery next week?

Thanks,
Danielle Park
Head of Infrastructure
Ironridge AI

---
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai>
To: Danielle Park <danielle@ironridge.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Ironridge on-site cluster intake: hardware inventory + first-run asks

Danielle —

Appreciate the context and attachments. I skimmed the inventory and rack map; we can make a tight POC that fits your constraints. Attaching a short draft runbook with the high-level decisions to review (provisioning-playbook-draft.md). Key points up front: 

1) Cluster composition (draft):
   - Control-plane: 3 dedicated m5-like nodes (no GPUs) for API/k8s control with dedicated NICs on management VLAN.
   - Worker pools: 
     * gpu-large: 2x nodes/rack with 2x A100 each (for inference serving), autoscaling target between 2-6 nodes depending on throughput.
     * gpu-burst: 1x smaller GPU node per rack for burst/eviction fallback.
   - Storage nodes: 1-2 blockstore target VMs (Ceph/RBD or external iSCSI) if you prefer central blockstore; otherwise, use NVMe local for checkpoints and replicate to an external archival target nightly.

2) Storage strategy:
   - Ephemeral KV/cache: use local NVMe on GPU workers (fastest).
   - Model artifacts & checkpoints: keep on replicated blockstore (RBD) with nightly snapshotting to a cold object store for DR.
   - If you need checkpoint durability without central blockstore, we can run a lightweight HA controller to push periodic checkpoints offsite.

3) Networking:
   - Management VLAN (control-plane) isolated from workload VLANs; BGP peering to your Direct Connect edge for egress rules.
   - Egress policy: route internet-bound inference telemetry through a dedicated NAT gateway in the VPC; model downloads can be restricted to a signed repository host.

4) Security/compliance:
   - KMS: we support Vault auto-rotation via our connector; will need service account + role mapping.
   - Audit logs: configure Fluentd to forward control-plane logs to your SIEM; Redwood will mirror inference audit events to a tenant log endpoint for 90-day retention.

Questions for you (quick):
- Do you prefer Ceph/RBD as the centralized blockstore or an external iSCSI appliance we can attach?
- Are you comfortable with control-plane on separate machines or do you prefer a co-located lightweight control-plane on the same racks?
- Any strict egress filtering (IP allowlist) that will block outbound test traffic during the POC?

Next steps: I’ll consolidate responses and produce a one-page runbook and a site checklist for the discovery call. Marissa — looping you for procurement / contract timeline input. Irene — could you check the Vault KMS integration plan and let us know any gaps?

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachment: provisioning-playbook-draft.md

---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai>
Cc: Danielle Park <danielle@ironridge.ai>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 13:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Ironridge on-site cluster intake: hardware inventory + first-run asks

Quick note from procurement side: Ironridge mentioned they want the POC covered under a short commercial addendum before we touch hardware on-site. Two specific asks: 

- Can we confirm a not-to-exceed for the 3-rack POC (approx estimate sufficient for PO)?
- They asked whether we offer reserved instance capacity for Dedicated later — if yes, they'd like ballpark pricing to evaluate with procurement.

Irene — any tech prerequisites that would block signing a preliminary PO? If not, I can draft an addendum and run it by legal. Mateo — once you confirm approximate BOM and service scope we can get a PO out.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

---
From: Danielle Park <danielle@ironridge.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 17 Nov 2027 14:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Ironridge on-site cluster intake: hardware inventory + first-run asks

Mateo / team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Short answers to your questions: 
- We have an iSCSI array in the back-of-rack for archival / blockstore (vendor: RackSupply). We can expose RBD if you recommend, but prefer iSCSI for initial POC.
- Control-plane: prefer dedicated non-GPU nodes (we want stronger isolation for the API plane).
- Egress: there is a strict allowlist for outbound from the management VLAN — I will provide the list by Friday.

Procurement: we can do a short PO for the POC. Ballpark NTE: $45k for three racks with labor. We’ll confirm after you share a BOM.

Irene — we’ll also share site power curves and BMS contact for the on-site engineer.

Talk on Friday — Danielle
